subject: Outbound guardrails and acceptance plan for Private Endpoint onboarding
messages:
From: Alex Chang <alex.chang@edgewarehealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood-inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private endpoint egress baseline + initial reqs

Hi Tessa,

We're preparing to flip traffic to Redwood Private (VPC) for our staging cluster next week and need to align on outbound network requirements so our firewall team can produce the ACLs and run a validation window. I've attached the spreadsheet with our internal constraints. High level asks below: 

- Allow outbound connections from our NAT to Redwood's private control-plane endpoints only (fqdn: private.redwood-inference.com and variants).
- Ports: 443 (TLS) for model control plane and telemetry; 5222 is used for legacy health pings in our environment — we can disable if you don't rely on it but want to double-check.
- IP granularity: we prefer a short list of static CIDRs to avoid per-host NAT rules. Can you provide the exact IPv4 ranges you expect egress to, and whether you support egress via customer NAT (no inbound)?
- TLS cert pinning: we run strict cert validation and will only allow outbound if you've published a current cert fingerprint or an expected CA chain.
- Proxy/inspection: our environment mandates a corporate outbound proxy for inspection. Will Redwood accept proxied outbound (CONNECT) to your endpoints, or do you require direct NAT egress?

Questions for our team:
- Can you confirm the minimum acceptance criteria for a short test window (connectivity + basic inference call + telemetry ingestion)?
- Are there any IPs for telemetry or background services that are separate from the control-plane FQDNs?

CC'ing Hannah and Dev for any Redwood IP lists and acceptance criteria. We can open a 3-hour maintenance window on Dec 2 if that helps.

Thanks,
Alex
CloudOps | Edgeware Health
Attachment: edgeware-egress-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Chang <alex.chang@edgewarehealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood-inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress baseline + initial reqs

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the spreadsheet. We can support both patterns (direct NAT egress or CONNECT through a corporate proxy) but there are slightly different acceptance checks for each path. Below are the concrete deliverables Redwood will provide and the acceptance criteria we'd like Edgeware to complete during the test window. 

Redwood deliverables (what we'll provide by EOD Dec 2):
- Small, static egress footprint: three IPv4 /24 ranges that host our private control-plane endpoints and telemetry collectors. (We will publish these as CSV and a signed JSON manifest with timestamp.)
- TLS details: SHA256 fingerprint for the control-plane certificate + the issuing CA chain (will be included in the manifest).
- Test runner: a short curl-based script (and a Python harness) that performs a control-plane handshake, a model->inference call (token-limited), and a telemetry ping.
- Fallback guidance: if proxy interception breaks telemetry, we can switch telemetry to an alternate port on the same IPs for the test window.

Edgeware acceptance criteria (recommended):
1) Firewall allowlist entries for the three /24 ranges to destination port 443 (egress) from your staging subnet(s).
2) Successful TLS handshake to private.redwood-inference.com where the cert fingerprint matches the manifest.
3) Successful inference call (sample prompt) with a response under 1s p50 latency in the staging region.
4) Telemetry ingestion check: we show the telemetry event in your tenant within 60s of the call.

Attachments I'm sending now: redwood-egress-sample-ips.csv (sample IPs, not the final manifest) and a short PDF that documents our egress policy and required cert validation steps (redwood-private-egress-policy.pdf).

If you prefer proxied egress, please tell us the proxy host/port and whether mutual TLS is required between your proxy and downstream hosts. For NAT egress, we'll publish the final /24s before the test window.

I'll schedule an internal pre-check with our NetOps folks — looping in Priyom for any routing/proxy edgecases.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-egress-sample-ips.csv, redwood-private-egress-policy.pdf

> Hi Tessa,
> 
> We're preparing to flip traffic to Redwood Private (VPC) for our staging cluster next week and need to align on outbound network requirements...

From: Alex Chang <alex.chang@edgewarehealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: cloudops@edgewarehealth.com, security@edgewarehealth.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress baseline + initial reqs

Tessa — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing your attachments: 

- Proxy: we'll do proxied egress during normal ops. During a 3-hour maintenance window we can switch to direct NAT for the staging subnet if that simplifies validation.
- mTLS: our proxy will not terminate mTLS to your endpoints; it will pass through CONNECT. No mutual TLS between proxy and external endpoints.
- NAT ranges: our firewall team prefers minimal /24s on their side as well. Please send the signed manifest for the three /24s.
- Telemetry: security asked whether telemetry payloads include any PII. We need a short note confirming telemetry is anonymized and that logs do not contain customer prompt text.

Requested point of contact: Janet Lee (firewall owner) at janet.lee@edgewarehealth.com — she's available for the Dec 2 window. We'll also open a support ticket (NETOPS-914) for the test. 

If you can publish the manifest and the test runner script by tonight we'll aim for the Dec 2 22:00–01:00 PST window for the direct-NAT validation.

Regards,
Alex
CloudOps | Edgeware Health

On Tue, 01 Dec 2026 at 11:04, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood-inference.com> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the spreadsheet. We can support both patterns...

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood-inference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood-inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood-inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Edgeware Health — egress ACL implementation and acceptance checklist (for sign-off)

Team — quick internal note after the exchange with Edgeware: below are the concrete steps we need to complete before we mark their onboarding as "network-approved." Please treat this as the runbook for the Dec 2–3 validation and include any comments inline.

Runbook / Implementation items:
- Publish final manifest (signed-manifest.json) with three /24 IPv4 ranges; attach to the Drive link and notify Alex. (Action: Tessa)
- Provide SHA256 cert fingerprint + CA chain to Edgeware security. (Action: Hannah)
- Push test harness (curl + python) to our onboarding repo; include expected curl returns & telemetry event id. (Action: Dev)
- Confirm proxy support caveat in docs: proxied egress via CONNECT is allowed but telemetry payloads must not be intercepted or altered (we'll provide a checksum header to detect modification). (Action: Priyom)
- Internal NetOps: validate that these IPs are only used by control plane / telemetry and are not resolving to customer-data storage endpoints. (NetOps)

Acceptance checklist for sign-off (Edgeware staging):
1) Firewall rules in Edgeware staging allow outbound to the three /24s on TCP/443.
2) TLS fingerprint from their curl run matches the manifest.
3) Inference call returns expected truncated response within 1s p50.
4) Telemetry event visible in onboarding tenant within 60s and payload checksum matches our groomed header.
5) Edgeware security confirms telemetry contains no PII and will not log prompts. (We require an email confirmation from security@edgewarehealth.com before sign-off.)

Notes / caveats:
- If their proxy rewrites TLS or terminates at the proxy, the acceptance test must be done via direct NAT during the window.
- If any telemetry pings are blocked by their inspection tooling, we'll provide an alternate telemetry port for the window (same IPs).
- We should avoid providing per-host IPs; keep the published manifest as the single source of truth.

I'll publish the manifest and the harness tonight. Priyom — can you add the checksum header to the telemetry spec and put a short verification snippet in the repo? Dev — once the harness is pushed, ping Janet Lee so Edgeware can run the test.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference
